**An exciting opportunity for an experienced CAD Co-ordinator to work in a high performing team environment**.

Every new building, refurbishment and transformed learning space at Macquarie University starts with accurate, reliable data. As our CAD Coordinator, you’ll play a key role in maintaining the digital information and technical systems that support the University’s built environment, enabling informed decisions across space planning, asset management and project design and delivery.

This is an exciting opportunity within our Property Division, with a newly reclassified role that reflects the growing technical expertise required across CAD, BIM/Revit and Archibus. You’ll have the opportunity to make a real impact by strengthening CAD standards and governance, improving processes, and contributing to automation and system integration initiatives across these platforms.

If you’re passionate about technical precision, digital innovation and improving the way information supports the built environment, this is your opportunity to shape the systems and standards behind the spaces where our university community learns, works and connects.

**About the Role**

Reporting to the Space Planning Data Manager, you will manage and develop the University's CAD database, Archibus system and BIM/Revit models, ensuring data integrity, system quality and accessible, accurate drawing and asset information. Your key accountabilities will include:

  

* Enabling space management and planning activity, including transmittal of BIM and CAD documentation for projects and planning (such as the Master Planning Campus Model), drafting CAD concept plans, sketches and diagrams, and contributing to space audits and furniture mapping across our Capus.
* Coordinating and administering 'as-built' CAD documentation received from consultant teams and contractors for inclusion in the University drawing database using AutoCAD (Autodesk).

* Managing the Archibus system, including data integrity, drawing integration and system quality assurance, and identifying, troubleshooting and resolving system issues or escalating where appropriate.
* Maintaining, reviewing and coordinating BIM and Revit models that inform planning, project delivery and asset management outcomes.
* Leading the development, implementation and monitoring of CAD design standards and procedures to meet customer requirements and industry benchmarks for continuous improvement.
* Developing and maintaining a central drawing database for authorised user access and assisting the wider Property Division with drawing and documentation requirements.
* Contributing to automation, process improvement and integration initiatives across the CAD, BIM and Archibus platforms, and providing ongoing and ad-hoc reporting and data visualisation of space utilisation.

The Property Division assists the University in achieving its learning, teaching and research goals through planning, development and maintenance services for all University buildings and infrastructure, as well as managing a growing commercial property investment portfolio. Please note that work hours may vary from time to time to accommodate business needs.

Macquarie University is a place of inspiration, a university known for its research excellence, progressive teaching and a campus set within 126 hectares of parkland. Our Property Division plays a defining part in that experience, planning and caring for the academic, research and commercial precincts that bring our community of students, researchers, clinicians and professional staff into one connected place. Here, technical expertise is valued, questions are welcomed, and good ideas are given room to grow.

**About You**

You are a CAD and BIM specialist who takes pride in accuracy, consistency and well-governed data. You enjoy being the person others rely on for the correct drawing, and you look for better ways to organise, automate and present information. You work comfortably with consultants and contractors, translate their documentation into university protocols, and explain technical detail in plain language to non-technical colleagues.

* Demonstrated experience administering and maintaining a CAD library and central drawing database, including data integrity and system quality assurance.
* Experience administering Archibus or an equivalent IWMS/space management platform, including troubleshooting and progressing system enhancements.
* Demonstrated ability to modify CAD drawing material provided by external consultants so that it complies with organisational protocols and standards.
* Well-developed written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear, accurate written material and to build effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
* Demonstrated ability to manage your own workload with minimal day-to-day direction within a multi-disciplinary team environment, and to keep pace with industry trends and developments in the CAD field.
* Experience in the higher education sector is desirable, though not essential.

Alzheimer's disease and epilepsy remain among the most complex challenges in neuroscience. At Macquarie University's Dementia Research Centre, researchers are working at the interface of molecular biology, animal models and cell-based systems to develop novel therapeutics for these disorders. We are seeking a Research Assistant to provide the research, technical and administrative expertise that keeps this work moving forward.

Reporting to A/Prof Janet van Eersel, you will be hands-on across the full research pipeline - from maintaining and characterising the mouse colony and conducting behavioural, motor and memory testing, through to molecular and biochemical analysis of tissue and cultured cells. **About the Department**
------------------------

The Department of Industry, Science and Resources and our broader portfolio are integral to the Australian Government’s economic agenda. Our purpose is to help the government build a better future for all Australians through enabling a productive, resilient and sustainable economy, enriched by science and technology. We do this by:

* Growing innovative & competitive businesses, industries and regions
* Investing in science and technology
* Strengthening the resources sector.

The APS and the department offer a clear direction and meaningful work. You will be able to create positive impact in people’s lives whilst contributing to improved outcomes for Australia and our people.

Please see the APSC’s APS Employee Value Proposition for more information on the benefits and value of employment within the APS.  

**About the team**
------------------

We are the Australian Government’s national authority on measurement.  
  
At the National Measurement Institute (NMI), we empower innovation and protect trust in Australian industry and society through world-class measurement science. Join a team where your expertise drives national impact, your curiosity is nurtured, and the work you do creates trusted measurement for a fair, safe, healthy and competitive Australia. Our employees enjoy career development opportunities, flexible working arrangements and the opportunity to shape Australia’s economic future through world-class measurement science.  
  
At NMI, precision meets purpose.  
  
We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We’re committed to building a diverse, inclusive and impactful workplace by hiring people who share our values and bring integrity, collaboration and innovation to everything they do.  
  
The Physical Metrology Branch develops, maintains and disseminates Australia’s peak physical measurement standards. It provides traceability assurance so measurements made in Australia are accepted internationally. Branch staff deliver calibration and other measurement services, contribute to international measurement forums and share expertise with Australian and international stakeholders.  
  
The Mass and Density Standards team maintains Australia’s primary standards and deliver the nation’s highest-level calibration services from milligrams to tonnes. Its work supports calibration and testing laboratories and sectors including advanced manufacturing, biomedical, defence and aerospace. The team operates within an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited quality system, develops and validates primary standards and automated calibration systems, and is advancing a new density measurement facility and research into an electrostatic force balance for improved sub-milligram measurement.

**The opportunity**
-------------------

Start or build your scientific or engineering career at Australia’s national measurement authority. With structured training and support from experienced scientists and engineers, you will develop specialist capability in precision mass and density measurement while contributing to nationally significant calibration services and Australia’s primary measurement standards.

**What’s in it for you?**
-------------------------

Join a community of professionals committed to technical measurement excellence and cutting-edge research. We invest in advanced facilities, foster collaboration with leading institutions and support innovation. You will work with people who have diverse skill sets including scientists, engineers, policy specialists and regulatory professionals.  
  
This role offers an early-career scientist or engineer a strong technical foundation in measurement science. You will receive practical training and develop valuable, transferable skills in complex measurement systems, instrumentation, data acquisition, measurement uncertainty and laboratory quality systems.  
  
As part of the Department of Industry, Science and Resources, employees at NMI are covered by an enterprise agreement and benefits include:

* Parental leave
* a vacation care subsidy
* $235 annual healthy lifestyle subsidy
* access to study assistance
* access to Employee Assistance Program - health, wellbeing, counselling and support when needed

**Our ideal candidate**
-----------------------

We are seeking an early-career scientist or engineer who is curious, practical and motivated to build specialist expertise in mass and density metrology. The role may also suit a laboratory technician or metrologist with relevant experience. You do not need prior expertise in mass and density measurement. Structured training, supervision and support will be provided as you develop capability and independence.  
  
You will:

* Demonstrate sound technical judgement, strong attention to detail and a commitment to producing accurate, high-quality work.
* Show initiative, curiosity and a willingness to learn and develop specialist skills in mass measurement and laboratory operations.
* Be comfortable working in a structured laboratory environment and applying quality, safety and accreditation requirements.
* Analyse technical information and data to solve problems, investigate issues and support evidence-based decisions.
* Take responsibility for delivering quality outcomes and maintaining the integrity of your work.
* Build productive working relationships and communicate technical information effectively.
* Work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
* Hold a tertiary qualification in physics, engineering or a related discipline, or have equivalent relevant laboratory experience.
* Experience with laboratory instrumentation, automation, programming or data acquisition systems such as Python, VBA or LabVIEW will be highly regarded.

We are looking for individuals who bring personal integrity and a sense of purpose, and who embody NMI's values of being Inclusive, Innovative, Accountable, Adaptable, Influential and Strategic.  
  
Our department has a commitment to inclusion and diversity, with an ambition of being the best possible place to work. This reflects the importance we place on our people and on creating a workplace culture where each and every one of us is valued and respected for our contribution. Our ideal candidate adds to this culture and our workplace in their own way.

**What you will do**
--------------------

Following training and working under limited direction within established laboratory, quality and safety frameworks, you will apply and continue to develop your professional and technical expertise to:

* Deliver timely, high-quality calibrations of weights, balances and hydrometers, and measurements of liquid and solid density and surface tension, using methods that support internationally recognised levels of accuracy.
* Plan and manage assigned calibration workflows, liaise with clients and resolve routine technical or scheduling issues to meet service agreements.
* Analyse measurement data, calculate and propagate uncertainty, interpret results and prepare clear technical records, reports and calibration documentation.
* Monitor equipment status, arrange calibrations and maintenance, and keep laboratory records accurate and current.
* Apply the ISO/IEC 17025 quality system and contribute to method documentation, validation, corrective action and continuous improvement.
* Investigate technical issues, diagnose equipment or process faults, and recommend and implement practical solutions within delegated authority.
* Contribute to the design, development and validation of new standards facilities, automated calibration systems and improvements to existing measurement systems.
* Contribute technical knowledge to team research and development activities, share information and adapt priorities to meet evolving client and business needs.

NMI values continuous learning and is committed to supporting staff to reach their full potential. In this role, you will have the opportunity to:

* Gain hands-on experience in a highly specialised and nationally significant area of measurement science, developing expertise in mass and density metrology through the calibration of weights, balances and hydrometers, and the measurement of liquid and solid density and surface tension.
* Build expertise in measurement uncertainty, traceability and quality systems within an ISO 17025-accredited laboratory.
* Apply your science or engineering skills to solve real-world measurement challenges across a range of industries.
* Collaborate with experienced scientists, engineers and metrologists on research and capability development projects that support Australia's national measurement infrastructure.

**Eligibility**
---------------

A tertiary qualification in physics, engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant laboratory experience, is required.

To be eligible for employment in the APS and the department, candidates must be Australian Citizens.

You don't need sales experience to join us. You need curiosity, drive and an interest in technology. We'll teach you the rest.

The SalesPond Graduate Program takes recent graduates with no prior sales experience and trains them to work as IT tech sales professionals. You'll learn on live B2B technology campaigns from your first weeks, supported by structured training through the SalesPond Academy, hands-on coaching from our Floor Managers, and an AI-enabled sales tech stack built to speed up your development.

SalesPond leads the way in bringing Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation into modern sales engagement. As a graduate here, you'll see first-hand how AI is changing the global B2B sales landscape, and you'll build skills that are in high demand across the tech industry.

Every graduate completes a structured training program so you're set up to succeed from day one:

* **SalesPond Academy:** formal training in B2B sales fundamentals, including prospecting, cold calling, qualification, objection handling, ideal customer profiles and how technology buyers make decisions.
* **AI tech stack training:** hands-on training in the AI and automation tools we use every day, for prospect research, call preparation, personalised outreach, sales acceleration and data management, so you learn to work faster and smarter.

You'll follow up with leads and talk with prospects to qualify them further, handle objections and, in most cases, set appointments for our clients' sales reps.

* Work closely with Floor Managers and Account Managers.
* Respond to customer requests for information.
* Stay knowledgeable and up to date on changes and developments in the B2B technology landscape.
* Keep management informed of all activity.

* Competently utilise Podiem, our Sales Engagement Platform.
* Take part in client meetings and briefings.

**Professional skills**

* Strong time management
* Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills
* Confident with computers, including MS Word, Excel, Outlook, Google Workspace and CRM databases
* Strong interest in technology and an active wish to master AI-driven sales engagement tools

**Personal attributes**

* Goal-oriented, self-motivated, confident, competitive, thorough and tenacious
* A fast learner who picks up new technologies quickly
* Coachable and open to feedback
* Trustworthy, professional and reliable with confidential information
* Composure, professionalism and attention to detail
* Integrity, timely decision-making and a drive for results
* Good planning, organising, reporting and networking skills

**Other skills and competencies**

* Proactive, outgoing and energetic
* Able to work independently within a team environment
* Comfortable on the phone, or keen to become comfortable
* Flexible and open to change
* Enthusiastic about meeting targets and able to stay composed under pressure

description_text:
**Your role**

You'll be part of our Office of General Counsel (OGC), which plays a critical role in supporting the firm's compliance, risk management and governance obligations. The team works closely with partners, lawyers and Corporate Services teams across the firm to maintain robust internal controls, manage professional obligations and support ethical and compliant business practices.

As a Business Administrator in our Office of General Counsel, you will:

* Coordinate a range of compliance, governance and risk administration processes, including securities trading requests, information barriers, practising certificate renewals and private work applications.
* Maintain accurate records, registers and databases to support the firm's compliance obligations, including conflicts, risk, certification and governance-related information.
* Support certification and admissions processes for lawyers and graduates, liaising with Law Societies and other external bodies to ensure regulatory requirements are met.
* Monitor shared inboxes, manage administrative workflows, coordinate approvals and follow up outstanding actions.
* Run reports and prepare information to assist the OGC team with compliance reviews, risk management activities and decision-making.
* Assist with conflicts administration, information barrier maintenance and data quality activities, identifying issues and escalating matters as appropriate.
* Provide administrative support for OGC matters, including file management, matter opening and closing, document filing and archiving.
* Work collaboratively with stakeholders across the firm while maintaining a high level of confidentiality, accuracy and professionalism.

This is a full-time, 12-month fixed-term contract opportunity. The role can be based in Brisbane, Melbourne, Perth or Sydney.

At Allens we have a hybrid working structure, typically 60% in the office and 40% from home. We would be happy to discuss any other flexible working arrangements that best support you.

**About you**

You are highly organised, detail-oriented and enjoy working in a structured environment where accuracy matters. You take pride in delivering high-quality administrative support and are comfortable managing multiple tasks while maintaining confidentiality.

You will have:

* Experience in administration, legal administration, professional services or compliance-related environments.
* Strong organisational skills and exceptional attention to detail.
* Experience maintaining records, databases, registers or business information systems.
* The ability to manage process-driven work accurately and consistently.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills and confidence working with a range of stakeholders.
* A proactive approach, with the ability to prioritise work, follow established processes and escalate issues appropriately.
* Intermediate Microsoft Office skills, particularly in Word and Excel.
* Experience supporting compliance, risk, governance or certification processes will be highly regarded but is not essential.
* A strong customer service mindset, excellent organisational capability and a commitment to accuracy.
* A desire to learn, grow, build relationships and contribute to a collaborative team environment.

You should also be comfortable handling confidential information, enjoy working with systems and processes, and be motivated by supporting a team that plays an important role in protecting the firm's professional and regulatory obligations.

**Your developmen**t

In joining Allens, you will receive unparalleled learning and development opportunities. You will be challenged, supported and guided as you learn and develop, and will be encouraged to grow. We foster greatness, and will coach and support you to meet your goals and aspirations.

**Our perks**

Our benefits include:

* **Financial**: market competitive fixed remuneration, employee recruitment referral program, discounts at hundreds of suppliers including retail outlets, health and travel insurance, charity matched funding program.
* **Health and wellbeing**: fully subsidised gym memberships, annual flu vaccinations, skin checks, in-house snacks and catered meals, subsidised sporting and social activities, Employee Assistance Program including confidential counselling, wellbeing coaching and financial coaching for employees and their families.
* **Flexibility**: hybrid and flexible working arrangements to support you in your work and life commitments and passions, equipment to support working from home.
* **Leave**: ability to purchase additional annual leave, access to an enhanced, inclusive and flexible parental leave policy – 26 weeks paid parental leave with no minimum service for permanent employees and high quality executive coaching to support the transition.
* **Recognition**: team based recognition including social activities and contribution based recognition activities, and annual Allens Values Awards to nominate and recognise the incredible contributions of our people.

Allens is also proud to invest in our communities, giving you the opportunity to make a difference through our work on reconciliation, the environment and other social justice issues as well as our workplace giving and volunteering programs.

**How to apply?**

We'd love to hear from you so please click "apply now"!

At Allens, our culture is made up of unique backgrounds and varying life experiences. We celebrate our people's differences across gender and gender identity, sexual orientation, age, ability, cultural backgrounds, First Nations communities, and family and caring arrangements. If you require adjustments to fully participate in our application process, please contact us at **careers@allens.com.au**. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds, so if you're excited about this role but your past experience doesn't align, please express your interest by emailing us at **careers@allens.com.au**. The right role for you might be just around the corner!

  

At Allens, we've been building legal careers for 200 years; longer than any other firm in Australia. The impact of our people extends to almost every sphere of business, government, the judiciary and the wider legal profession. We continue to provide opportunities for people from diverse backgrounds to build outstanding careers and shape the world around them.

Through our alliance with Linklaters, we work in a global network of 40 offices in 25 countries. Our size and global reach provide exceptional opportunities for career development, including both on-the-job learning and formal training and development opportunities.

Our commitment to high performance is balanced with a focus on wellbeing, with a culture that's inclusive, supportive and collaborative. We prioritise connection and value the unique contribution of everyone at the firm.

We're proud to hold some of the world's longest ongoing client relationships, stretching back more than 180 years.

Imagine thriving in a team environment that positively impacts the community and drives clean energy change! Are you passionate about a cleaner and greener future?

At National Carbon Bank of Australia (NCBA), we’re committed to our team members’ development, job satisfaction and rewarding our people. Join our team to grow alongside a successful business and flourishing industry.

**Are you a university graduate looking for an exciting kick start to your career in the environment, renewables & green energy space? This opportunity has your name on it!**

* Environmental Science/Climate/Sustainability/Renewable Energy Graduate Opportunity (completed bachelor’s degree)

* Development and growth opportunities within the role
* Start as soon as possible

Join our NCBA team and help clients minimise the financial burden of installing renewable energy systems, enabling homeowners and businesses to lower their energy bills and reduce their carbon footprint.

We work with government energy efficiency schemes, including the NSW Energy Savings Scheme (ESS) and Peak Demand Reduction Scheme (PDRS), to identify eligible renewable energy and energy-saving opportunities for our clients. * Advising and consulting with clients to resolve issues with certificate creations, help with enquiries and in particular assist with client use of our online platforms and requests for information on forms.
* Validating compliance documentation and liaising with clients to document collection requirements.
* Update and maintain department processing manuals and contribute to process improvements.

**We offer:**

* A flexible work environment supporting working-from-home opportunities as well as increasing paid non-workdays off (Wellness Days) as service milestones are met.
* Participation in our annual profit-share employee incentive program.
* Paid public transportation incentive program.
* A fantastic open office space located in North Sydney with additional features including an on-site cafe, a table tennis table, parking availability on certain days of the week, and terrific social catchups and networking.
* A collaborative work environment with an open and honest culture and a team who are passionate about the energy efficiency sector.
* A leadership team committed to helping you succeed with decades of experience servicing customers in the environmental and renewable energy markets.
* The opportunity to grow with the largest certificate creator in Australia with offices in both Victoria and New South Wales.
* Commitment to your personal and professional learning and development with opportunities for growth.

**What we are looking for:**

We are looking for someone who:

* An university degree in environmental industry or similar area of study is an advantage.
* Prior customer service experience in any sector is advantageous.
* A proactive, self-motivated and goal-driven personality with a desire to step up and take on additional responsibility.
* Strong use of initiative and analytical skills when resolving problems with customers and team members.
* General competency with picking up technical systems & platforms, alongside an understanding of the Microsoft Suite of applications, including Outlook.
* Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy in terms of compliance, governance and risk management.
* Excellent written communication skills, with demonstrated ability to structure clear, polished and appropriately formal client communications, particularly via email.
* The ability to explore needs through listening and having consultative conversations. Is confident communicating on the phone and meeting face to face.
* The ability to plan, manage and prioritise your time.

If this sounds like you and you'd like to have a confidential chat, then we'd love to hear from you!

**How to Apply:**

Please submit your application through Indeed.

To be considered, please attach a CV with all relevant experience and **a cover letter detailing what you will bring to the team and how you can make our business better.**
